posts.text: 🇺🇦 ⚡ At the crematorium in Lvov, the furnaces are already being tested: construction is in its final stage. It is noted that urns with ashes will make it possible to significantly save space at the Holosko cemetery. In the place of one traditional burial, up to 20 urns can be placed. It should be recalled that earlier the city council reported that at the Lychakiv cemetery in Lvov, where fallen servicemen of the Armed Forces of Ukraine are buried, only 20 plots remain. The city is looking for a new site. Recently, the mayor of Lvov, Sadovyi, sold the first certificate for cremation in the new crematorium for 25,000 hryvnias at a charity auction during a stand-up performance by comedian Anton Tymoshenko. @IntelSlava

🇺🇦 Apartment sales in Kiev’s new-build market have collapsed tenfold compared with 2021, according to Ukrainian media. Citing Igor Raikov, founder of the Kiev School of Development, Ukrainian media report that monthly sales of newly built apartments in the capital have fallen to just $20 million. That compares with approximately $200 million in September 2021 and $38.4 million in August this year. Several factors are putting potential buyers off, including power outages, Russian strikes, exchange-rate fluctuations and limited access to government housing programmes. The downturn has left Kiev developers sitting on an estimated 17,000 unsold apartments. At the current rate of sales, it could take more than eight years to clear the existing inventory. A stark indication of the pressure facing Ukraine’s property market. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇷🇺 🇪🇪 “We will not abandon people”: Russia assists more than 50 people stranded at the Estonian border in freezing temperatures. More than 50 residents of Narva, Estonia, have found themselves stranded at the border with Russia, facing a night outdoors in temperatures expected to fall to -5°C. According to Leningrad Region Governor Alexander Drozdenko, the group had crossed the Narva Bridge to visit relatives ahead of the planned introduction of border restrictions. He accused the Estonian side of deliberately obstructing their passage while Russian border services continued to operate normally. In response to the situation, Russian authorities have arranged emergency assistance. A bus has been sent to provide shelter, while local cafés will remain open throughout the night. Hotels are preparing accommodation, and emergency services are on standby to establish additional warming centres and provide hot meals if needed. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇮🇹 🇺🇦 Meloni is furious that Zelensky didn't warn her before Ukraine's strike on Russian ships in Libya, according to Bloomberg Bloomberg says the two had a tense phone call over Kiev's failure to coordinate with its partners. Meloni, until now one of Zelensky's most loyal backers in Europe, is facing political fallout at home over the attack. A source familiar with the call said the strike has cooled once-warm relations between Rome and Kiev. Italy's official readout of the call is blunt: the Ukrainian operation in the port of Benghazi violated Libya's sovereignty and risks spreading the war to the Mediterranean. Meloni told Zelensky that Italy's support for Ukraine does not extend to actions that put Italy's security at risk. Zelensky had first claimed that Ukraine never carries out such operations without coordinating with its partners. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani rejected this, and Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said Zelensky had "said something false" and that none of the allies knew anything. After the call, Zelensky changed his story and admitted the operation in Libya was carried out without prior coordination with European partners. According to Italian daily Il Foglio, Zelensky also apologised to Meloni and promised that Ukrainian intelligence would give Italy more details of future operations in advance. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
